idiom_name: component is ITextAccessor ta / component as IFormattable
implementation_notes: An interface in C# is already a separate, client-sized contract, so growing a component's surface means declaring another interface and probing for it: component is ITextAccessor ta discriminates and binds in one step (C# 7 pattern form), component as IFormattable returns null instead of throwing, and the extension is the object itself rather than an adapter. The framework design rule 'DO NOT add members to an interface that has previously shipped' is the pattern's motivation in writing, and IServiceProvider.GetService(Type) is the same total query when capabilities live in a container rather than on the object.
pitfalls: as returns null and the following member access throws NullReferenceException: check the result, and prefer the is-pattern form that binds only on success.
Probing boxes struct implementors on every cast; cache or push the capability into a generic constraint in hot paths.
Adding an abstract member to a shipped public interface is a binary-breaking change for every existing implementor - the reason to probe for a new interface instead.

variants.name: Default interface members (C# 8 virtual extension methods)
variants.idiom_name: interface member with a default body + protected static helper
variants.implementation_notes: When the extension belongs on the base interface itself and a sensible default exists, C# 8 default interface members add the member without breaking implementors: existing classes compile unchanged and take the default, an implementor may override it, and interface-typed callers see the new member - the language-level answer to additive interface evolution. This replaces the lookup where a default is meaningful, but the member is reachable only through the interface type and its default body can use only the interface's other members, so extensions that need extra state or an adapter still use probing.
pitfalls: Default members are not inherited by the implementing type: a concrete-typed reference does not see them - the call must be made through the interface.
The default body cannot reach the implementor's own state, so only extensions expressible in terms of existing interface members can use this variant.
Explicit base-interface invocation (base(IFoo).M()) was not implemented in C# 8; a diamond of default implementations must resolve to one most-specific member.
